hindi: उन छह रसों की योनि जल है। छेदन और उपशमन, ये दो कर्म हैं; उन दोनों के मिश्रण से साधारणता होती है। स्वादुता और अस्वादुता रुचि है; हित और अहित प्रभाव हैं। आश्रय तो पाँच महाभूतों के विकार हैं, जो प्रकृति, विकृति, विचार, देश और काल के अधीन हैं। द्रव्य नाम वाले उन आश्रयों में गुरु, लघु, शीत, उष्ण, स्निग्ध, रूक्ष आदि गुण होते हैं। क्षरण के कारण क्षार (कहलाता है); वह रस नहीं है; वह द्रव्य है, जो अनेक रसों से उत्पन्न, अनेक रसों वाला, अधिकतर कटु और लवण, अनेक इन्द्रियार्थों से युक्त और करण से निर्मित है। रसों की अव्यक्तता तो प्रकृति में, अनुरस में, अथवा अनुरस से युक्त द्रव्य में होती है। फिर, उन आश्रय आदि भावों के विशेषों के असंख्येय होने के कारण (रसों की) असंख्येयता ठीक नहीं है; क्योंकि इन आश्रय आदि भावों में से एक-एक भी विशेषों को ग्रहण करता है, क्योंकि विशेष असंख्येय हैं, और उससे (रस का) अन्यत्व सिद्ध नहीं होता, क्योंकि ये अधिकतर परस्पर संसृष्ट रहते हैं; और उत्पत्ति के कारण इन गुणप्रकृति वालों की असंख्येयता नहीं होती। इसलिए बुद्धिमान् संसृष्ट रसों का कर्म नहीं बताते।
english: Of these six tastes the source is water. Cutting and pacifying are the two actions; from the mixing of the two comes commonness (sādhāraṇatva). Palatability and unpalatability are (a matter of) liking (bhakti); wholesome and unwholesome are the effects (prabhāva). The substrata (āśraya), however, are modifications of the five great elements, dependent on nature, modification, vicāra, place and time. In these substrata, called substances (dravya), are the qualities (guṇa) heavy, light, cold, hot, unctuous, dry and the rest. Alkali (kṣāra) is so called from wearing away (kṣaraṇa); it is not a taste: it is a substance, produced from many tastes, having many tastes, mostly pungent and salty, accompanied by many sense-objects, produced by a process (karaṇa). Unmanifestness of the tastes, however, occurs in their source (prakṛti), in the subsidiary taste (anurasa), or in a substance accompanied by a subsidiary taste. Again, countlessness (of the tastes) because the particulars of those entities, the substrata and the rest, are countless is not proper: for each one of these entities, the substrata and the rest, takes on particulars, since particulars are countless, and otherness (of taste) does not follow from that, because they are for the most part combined with one another; nor does countlessness arise, from their production, for these (tastes) whose nature is qualities. Therefore the intelligent do not teach the action of combined tastes.

text_flags.why: 'aparisaṃkhyeyeatva' is not a form (stray e before atva); the same compound is printed correctly as viśeṣāparisaṃkhyeyatvāt later in this unit
'veśeṣa' is not a word; viśeṣa (particular) is the word used throughout this unit (viśeṣāparisaṃkhyeyatvāt in the same sentence)

notes: The unit answers the views of units 8 and P1 to P7 point by point (water, cutting/pacifying, commonness, palatability, wholesomeness, the five elements, the qualities, kṣāra, avyakta, countlessness). vicāra in prakṛtivikṛtivicāra- is kept in Sanskrit: its sense here (consideration, combination or processing) is not certain from the chunk. prakṛti 'source' may refer to the source water named at the start of the unit or to the original state; anurase may mean 'in (a substance where the taste is only) subsidiary'. The attachment of parasparasaṃsṛṣṭabhūyiṣṭhatvāt is ambiguous: it is taken as the reason for 'otherness does not follow'; it can also be read as the reason for the following clause. guṇaprakṛtīnām is taken as a bahuvrīhi 'whose nature is qualities' agreeing with eṣām (the tastes); a reading 'of the qualities and natures' is possible, so this clause is uncertain. karaṇa 'process' = preparation by a procedure; the ';' attached to karaṇābhinirvṛttam is left out of the split. Review: anurase is read as the noun 'in the subsidiary taste' (m. loc. sg.), a third locus beside prakṛtau and dravye; an adjective of dravye ('a substance of subsidiary taste') remains possible. ekaikaḥ may also be each single taste, with eṣām āśrayādīnāṃ bhāvānām depending on viśeṣān ('each taste takes on the particulars of these entities'). text_flags viśeṣāparisaṃkhyeyeatva → -saṃkhyeyatva and veśeṣān → viśeṣān accepted (non-words; correct forms printed in the same unit).

english: In this context every substance is made of the five elements (pāñcabhautika); it is sentient and insentient. Its qualities are sound and the rest, and heavy and the rest ending with fluid (drava); action is stated to be fivefold, emesis and the rest.

hindi: उनमें जो द्रव्य गुरु, खर, कठिन, मन्द, स्थिर, विशद, सान्द्र, स्थूल और गन्ध गुणों की बहुलता वाले हैं, वे पार्थिव हैं; वे उपचय, संघात, गुरुता और स्थिरता करते हैं। जो द्रव, स्निग्ध, शीत, मन्द, मृदु, पिच्छिल और रस गुणों की बहुलता वाले हैं, वे आप्य हैं; वे उपक्लेद, स्नेह, बन्ध, विष्यन्द, मृदुता और प्रसन्नता करते हैं। जो उष्ण, तीक्ष्ण, सूक्ष्म, लघु, रूक्ष, विशद और रूप गुणों की बहुलता वाले हैं, वे आग्नेय हैं; वे दाह, पाक, प्रभा, प्रकाश और वर्ण करते हैं। जो लघु, शीत, रूक्ष, खर, विशद, सूक्ष्म और स्पर्श गुणों की बहुलता वाले हैं, वे वायव्य हैं; वे रूक्षता, ग्लानि, विचरण, विशदता और लघुता करते हैं। जो मृदु, लघु, सूक्ष्म, श्लक्ष्ण और शब्द गुणों की बहुलता वाले हैं, वे आकाशात्मक हैं; वे मृदुता, सुषिरता और लघुता करते हैं।
english: Among them, substances abounding in the qualities heavy, rough, hard, slow, stable, non-slimy, dense, gross and smell are earthy (pārthiva); they produce increase (upacaya), compactness, heaviness and stability. Those abounding in the qualities fluid, unctuous, cold, slow, soft, slimy and taste are watery (āpya); they produce moistening (upakleda), unctuousness, binding, liquefaction (viṣyanda), softness and refreshment. Those abounding in the qualities hot, sharp, subtle, light, dry, non-slimy and form (rūpa) are fiery (āgneya); they produce burning, pāka (cooking, digestion), lustre, light and colour. Those abounding in the qualities light, cold, dry, rough, non-slimy, subtle and touch are airy (vāyavya); they produce dryness, weariness (glāni), movement (vicāra), non-sliminess and lightness. Those abounding in the qualities soft, light, subtle, smooth and sound are of the nature of space (ākāśa); they produce softness, porosity and lightness.

hindi: किन्तु द्रव्य केवल गुणों के प्रभाव से ही कार्यकारी नहीं होते; क्योंकि द्रव्य, द्रव्य के प्रभाव से, गुणों के प्रभाव से और द्रव्य तथा गुणों के प्रभाव से, उस-उस काल में, उस-उस अधिकरण को पाकर, उस-उस युक्ति और उस-उस प्रयोजन को लक्ष्य करके जो करते हैं, वह कर्म है; जिससे करते हैं, वह वीर्य है; जहाँ करते हैं, वह अधिकरण है; जब करते हैं, वह काल है; जैसे करते हैं, वह उपाय है; जो सिद्ध करते हैं, वह फल है।
english: But substances are not effective through the power (prabhāva) of their qualities alone; for what substances do, through the power of the substance, through the power of the qualities, and through the power of substance and qualities, at this or that time, having reached this or that site, with regard to this or that rational planning (yukti) and this or that purpose, that is action (karma); that by which they do it is potency (vīrya); where they do it is the site (adhikaraṇa); when they do it is the time (kāla); how they do it is the means (upāya); what they accomplish is the result (phala).

notes: tara and tama are the comparative and superlative suffixes, used as nouns for degrees of intensity; taratama may also be read as a neuter dvandva.

hindi: संयोग सत्तावन हैं, किन्तु कल्पना तिरसठ प्रकार की है; वहाँ रसों की योग्यता के कारण रस का चिन्तन करने वालों ने (इसे) कल्पित किया है।
english: The combinations are fifty-seven, but the arrangement (kalpanā) is sixty-threefold; it has been devised by those who reflect on tastes, because of the suitability of the tastes there.
notes: fifty-seven = the combinations of two or more tastes (15 + 20 + 15 + 6 + 1); with the 6 single tastes the arrangement is 63 (unit 22). tatra 'there' is taken as 'in that matter' (in the arrangement or its use).

words.gram: m. acc. pl., bahuvrīhi with dvandva

hindi: सिद्धि चाहने वाले वैद्य को दोष, औषध आदि का विचार करके कहीं एक रस की कल्पना करनी चाहिए और कहीं संयुक्त रसों की।
english: A physician who desires success, after considering doṣa, medicine and the rest, is to employ a single taste in some cases and combined tastes in others.

text_flags.why: 'aiṣadha' is not a word; doṣa + auṣadha (medicine) gives doṣauṣadha by sandhi, and the line keeps 16 syllables either way

hindi: बुद्धिमान् रोगों के प्रति दो रसों आदि वाले द्रव्यों की, और संयुक्त रसों की, अथवा एक-एक रस की भी कल्पना करते हैं।
english: The wise employ, against diseases, substances of two tastes and the rest, and combined tastes, or also tastes one by one.
notes: vā api is rendered 'or also' (Hindi अथवा ... भी).

words.gloss: knower of the gradations of tastes

hindi: जो रसों के विकल्पों का ज्ञाता हो और दोषों के विकल्पों का ज्ञाता हो, वह विकारों के हेतु, लिङ्ग और उपशान्ति के विषय में मोहित नहीं होगा।
english: He who knows the gradations (vikalpa) of tastes and knows the gradations of the doṣas would not be confused about the causes, signs and alleviation of disorders.

hindi: सूखे द्रव्य का और आरम्भ में द्रव्य का रस व्यक्त लक्षित होता है; इसके विपरीत होने पर अनुरस होता है; क्योंकि सातवाँ रस नहीं है।
english: The taste of a substance, when it is dry and at the beginning, is perceived as manifest; in the reverse case it is the subsidiary taste (anurasa); for there is no seventh taste.

text_flags.why: 'rso' (r with no vowel before s) is not a word; rasaḥ (taste) fits the sense; metre: with raso the even pāda ra-so-nā-sti-hi-sap-ta-maḥ has 8 syllables and syllables 5-7 hi-sap-ta are light-heavy-light as an even anuṣṭubh pāda needs; with rso it has 7

notes: 'at the beginning' (ādau) is taken as the first perception of the taste; vyaktaḥ is taken as predicative with lakṣyate ('is perceived as manifest'). The opposite (viparyayeṇa) is taken as 'not manifest, in the dry state or at the beginning'.
lines_deva: व्यक्तः शुष्कस्य चादौ च रसो द्रव्यस्य लक्ष्यते
lines_iast: vyaktaḥ śuṣkasya cādau ca raso dravyasya lakṣyate

hindi: परत्व और अपरत्व, और युक्ति, संख्या और संयोग, और विभाग, और पृथक्त्व, और परिमाण भी,
english: Remoteness and nearness (paratva and aparatva), rational planning (yukti), number, conjunction, disjunction, separateness and also measure,
notes: SENTENCE: this list has no verb and continues beyond this unit, which is the last of the chunk. parāparatve is a dvandva in the dual (paratva and aparatva), the -tva of the second member serving both. paratva/aparatva may also mean 'superiority and inferiority'; 'remoteness and nearness' is the literal sense. eva in saṃyoga eva ca is a filler emphatic, not translated separately.
lines_deva: परापरत्वे युक्तिश्च संख्या संयोग एव च
lines_iast: parāparatve yuktiśca saṃkhyā saṃyoga eva ca

hindi: संस्कार और अभ्यास: ये परादि गुण जानने चाहिए, जो चिकित्सा की सिद्धि के उपाय हैं; उन्हें हम उनके लक्षणों द्वारा बताते हैं।
english: Saṃskāra (processing) and abhyāsa (repeated practice): these are to be known as the qualities beginning with para, the means of success in treatment; we describe them by their characteristics.
notes: SENTENCE: the list of the qualities beginning with para starts in the previous unit (29) and ends here with saṃskāra and abhyāsa.

words.gloss: in place, time, age, measure, vipāka, vīrya, taste and so on
words.gram: n. loc. pl., bahuvrīhi (dvandva first members)

hindi: देश, काल, वय, मान, पाक, वीर्य, रस आदि के विषय में परत्व और अपरत्व होते हैं; और युक्ति वह योजना है जो उपयुक्त हो।
english: Paratva and aparatva (remoteness and nearness) are with respect to place, time, age, measure, vipāka (post-digestive effect), vīrya (potency), taste and so on; and yukti (rational planning) is the combining (yojanā) that is fitting.
notes: The verb for para-apara is understood; parāparatve read as nominative dual (paratva and aparatva). pāka here is taken as vipāka. Alternative sense of parāparatva: superiority and inferiority.

words.gloss: born of the action of two, of all or of one
words.gram: m. nom. sg., upapada tat-puruṣa (dvandva first members)

hindi: संख्या गणना है; द्रव्यों का साथ मिलना संयोग कहा जाता है, जो दो के, सबके या एक के कर्म से उत्पन्न होता है और अनित्य ही है।
english: Saṃkhyā (number) is counting; the union together of substances is called saṃyoga (conjunction); it is born of the action of two, of all or of one, and is indeed non-eternal.
notes: dravyāṇāṃ is taken with saha yogaḥ (union of substances together).
lines_deva: संख्या स्याद्गणितं योगः सह संयोग उच्यते
lines_iast: saṃkhyā syādgaṇitaṃ yogaḥ saha saṃyoga ucyate

hindi: विभाग तो विभक्ति, वियोग और भाग-भाग करके ग्रहण है; पृथक्त्व असंयोग, विलक्षणता और अनेकता है।
english: Vibhāga (disjunction) is division, separation, taking part by part; pṛthaktva (separateness) is non-conjunction, difference of characteristics, multiplicity.

hindi: परिमाण मान है; संस्कार करण माना गया है; अभ्यास भाव का बार-बार आवर्तन, शीलन और निरन्तर क्रिया है।
english: Parimāṇa (measurement) is measure; saṃskāra (processing) is held to be the making (karaṇa); abhyāsa (repeated practice) is the repetition of a state, habituation, constant practice.
notes: punaḥ is taken as a connective ("again", "and"); it is left untranslated in Hindi.

hindi: इस प्रकार परादि सभी गुण उनके अपने लक्षणों सहित कहे गए, जिन्हें न जानने पर चिकित्सा ठीक प्रकार से नहीं चलती।
english: Thus all the qualities beginning with para have been stated with their own characteristics; when they are not known, treatment does not proceed properly.
notes: yair aviditaiḥ: instrumental absolute sense, "these not being known".

hindi: गुणों को गुणों के आश्रित नहीं कहा गया है; इसलिए वैद्य रस के गुणों को द्रव्य के गुण जाने। कर्ता के अभिप्राय अनेक प्रकार के होते हैं।
english: Qualities are not said to have qualities as their support; therefore the physician should know the qualities of the tastes as the qualities of the substances. The intentions of the author are of various kinds.
notes: SENTENCE: the last clause (kartur abhiprāyāḥ pṛthagvidhāḥ) leads into the next unit.

english: And therefore, having understood the matter in hand, the differences of place and time, the intentions of the author of the treatise and the means, one should declare the meaning.

english: Next after this I shall declare the six divisions of the tastes, and how the six tastes, arising from the five elements, are enumerated.

hindi: जल निश्चय ही सौम्य, अन्तरिक्ष में उत्पन्न, स्वभाव से शीतल, लघु और अव्यक्त रस वाले होते हैं; वे अन्तरिक्ष से गिरते हुए और गिरकर पाँच महाभूतों के गुणों से युक्त होकर जंगम और स्थावर प्राणियों के शरीरों को तृप्त करते हैं; उन शरीरों में छह रस प्रकट होते हैं।
english: The waters are indeed saumya (of the nature of soma), arising in the atmosphere, cold by nature, light and of unmanifest taste; while falling from the atmosphere and having fallen, endowed with the qualities of the five great elements, they nourish the bodies of mobile and immobile beings; in those bodies the six tastes take shape.

hindi: इन छह रसों में सोम के गुण की अधिकता से मधुर रस, पृथ्वी और अग्नि की प्रधानता से अम्ल, जल और अग्नि की प्रधानता से लवण, वायु और अग्नि की प्रधानता से कटु, वायु और आकाश की अधिकता से तिक्त, और पवन तथा पृथ्वी की अधिकता से कषाय रस होता है।
english: Of these six tastes, the sweet taste comes from excess of the quality of soma; the sour from predominance of earth and fire; the salty from predominance of water and fire; the pungent from predominance of air and fire; the bitter from excess of air and space (ākāśa); and the astringent from excess of air (pavana) and earth.

english: Among them, the tastes made of fire and air (māruta) mostly tend upward, owing to the lightness and upward floating of air and the upward flaming of fire; those made of water and earth mostly tend downward, owing to the heaviness of earth and the downward course of water; and those of mixed nature tend both ways.
notes: Prose passage typed as a verse unit (one long line). māruta and vāyu here are the element air, not the doṣa Vāta. ūrdhvabhāj/adhobhāj: literally "sharing in the upward/downward"; rendered "tending upward/downward".
lines_deva: तत्राग्निमारुतात्मका रसाः प्रायेणोर्ध्वभाजः लाघवादुत्प्लवनत्वाच्च वायोरूर्ध्वज्वलनत्वाच्च वह्नेः सलिलपृथिव्यात्मकास्तु प्रायेणाधोभाजः पृथिव्या गुरुत्वान्निम्नगत्वाच्चोदकस्य व्यामिश्रात्मकाः पुनरुभयतोभाजः

hindi: उनमें मधुर रस शरीर के अनुकूल होने से रस, रुधिर, मांस, मेद, अस्थि, मज्जा, ओज और शुक्र को बढ़ाने वाला, आयु के लिए हितकर, छहों इन्द्रियों को प्रसन्न करने वाला, बल और वर्ण देने वाला, पित्त, विष और मारुत का नाश करने वाला, तृष्णा और दाह को शान्त करने वाला, त्वचा के लिए हितकर, केशों के लिए हितकर, कण्ठ के लिए हितकर, बलकारी, प्रीणन, जीवन, तर्पण, बृंहण, स्थिरता देने वाला, क्षीण और क्षत को जोड़ने वाला, नाक, मुख, कण्ठ, होंठ और जीभ को आनन्द देने वाला, दाह और मूर्च्छा को शान्त करने वाला, भौंरों और चींटियों को सबसे प्रिय, स्निग्ध, शीतल और गुरु होता है।
english: Among them, the sweet taste, because of its suitability to the body, increases rasa, blood, flesh, fat, bone, marrow, ojas (vital essence) and semen; it promotes life, clears the six sense faculties, produces strength and complexion, destroys Pitta, poison and Vāta (māruta), allays thirst and burning, is good for the skin, the hair and the throat, is strengthening, gladdening, vitalizing, replenishing (tarpaṇa) and nourishing, gives firmness, unites the wasted and the wounded, delights the nose, mouth, throat, lips and tongue, allays burning and mūrcchā (fainting), is most liked by bees and ants, and is unctuous, cold and heavy.

hindi: ऐसे गुणों वाला होने पर भी वह अकेला ही अत्यधिक सेवन किए जाने पर स्थूलता, मृदुता, आलस्य, अतिनिद्रा, भारीपन, अन्न की इच्छा का अभाव, अग्नि की दुर्बलता, मुख और कण्ठ में मांस की वृद्धि, तथा श्वास, कास, प्रतिश्याय, अलसक, शीतज्वर, आनाह, मुख की मधुरता, वमथु, संज्ञा और स्वर का नाश, गलगण्ड, गण्डमाला, श्लीपद, गले का शोफ, बस्ति, धमनियों और गले पर लेप, नेत्ररोग और अभिष्यन्द, इस प्रकार के कफज विकारों को उत्पन्न करता है।
english: Though it has such qualities, when used alone and excessively it produces corpulence (sthaulya), softness, lassitude, excessive sleep, heaviness, lack of desire for food, weakness of the digestive fire, growth of flesh in the mouth and throat, and Kapha-born disorders such as dyspnoea, cough, coryza (pratiśyāya), alasaka, cold fever, distension (ānāha), sweetness of the mouth, vomiting (vamathu), loss of consciousness and of voice, galagaṇḍa, gaṇḍamālā, ślīpada, swelling of the throat, coating of the bladder, vessels and throat, eye disease and abhiṣyanda.

text_flags.why: gaṇda with dental d is not a word; the same compound prints galagaṇḍa just before; read gaṇḍamālā

notes: Disease names kept Sanskrit (alasaka, galagaṇḍa, gaṇḍamālā, ślīpada, abhiṣyanda), no identifications. saṃjñāsvarapraṇāśa is read as one item "loss of consciousness and of voice". bastidhamanīgalopalepa is read as one item "coating of bladder, vessels and throat". The long dvandva is given as one word for the split. Whether the first nine items (sthaulya ... māṃsābhivṛddhi) are also counted among the Kapha-born disorders is not decided by the line; the translation keeps them as separate objects of upajanayati.

english: The sour taste makes food relished, kindles the digestive fire (agni), nourishes the body, invigorates, awakens the mind, makes the senses firm, increases strength, moves Vāta downward, refreshes the heart, makes the mouth water, moves down what has been eaten, moistens, digests, gladdens, and is light, hot and unctuous.

hindi: ऐसे गुणों वाला होने पर भी वह अकेला ही अत्यधिक सेवन किए जाने पर दाँतों में सिहरन लाता है, प्यास उत्पन्न करता है, दोनों आँखें मुँदवाता है, रोंगटे खड़े करता है, कफ को पिघलाता है, पित्त को बढ़ाता है, रक्त को दूषित करता है, मांस में दाह करता है, शरीर को शिथिल करता है, क्षीण, क्षत, कृश और दुर्बल लोगों में श्वयथु उत्पन्न करता है; और भी, अपने आग्नेय स्वभाव के कारण क्षत, चोट खाए, काटे हुए, जले, टूटे, सूजे, अपने स्थान से हटे, जिन पर मूत्र किया गया हो, जिन पर रेंगा गया हो, मसले गए, कटे, फटे, अलग हुए, बिंधे और कुचले हुए आदि भागों में पाक उत्पन्न करता है, और कण्ठ, छाती तथा हृदय में जलन करता है।
english: Though it has such qualities, when used alone and excessively it sets the teeth on edge, causes thirst, makes the eyes close, makes the body hairs bristle, liquefies Kapha, increases Pitta, vitiates the blood, burns the flesh, makes the body lax, and brings about swelling (śvayathu) in the wasted, wounded, lean and weak; moreover, because of its fiery nature, it causes pāka (inflammation) in what is wounded, struck, bitten, burnt, broken, swollen, dislocated, urinated upon, crept over, crushed, cut, split, separated, pierced, pounded and the like, and it burns the throat, chest and heart.

hindi: लवण रस पाचन, क्लेदन, दीपन, च्यावन, छेदन, भेदन, तीक्ष्ण, सर, विकासी, नीचे की ओर सरकाने वाला, अवकाश करने वाला, वातहर, स्तम्भ, बन्ध और संघात को दूर करने वाला, सब रसों का विरोधी होता है; वह मुख में पानी लाता है, कफ को द्रवित करता है, मार्गों को शुद्ध करता है, शरीर के सब अवयवों को मृदु करता है, आहार में रुचि उत्पन्न करता है, आहार के साथ जुड़ने वाला है, और बहुत गुरु नहीं होता, तथा स्निग्ध और उष्ण होता है।
english: The salty taste is digesting, moistening, stimulating digestion, dislodging, cutting, breaking, sharp, flowing, spreading, moving downward, making space, Vāta-removing, dispersing stiffness, binding and compaction, and opposed to all the tastes; it makes the mouth water, liquefies Kapha, cleanses the passages, softens all the parts of the body, makes food relished, goes with food, and is not excessively heavy, and is unctuous and hot.

text_flags.why: possible: dikāsin is not a word; vikāsin (spreading) fits this list of actions; d/v confusion of the print

notes: Prose passage typed as a verse unit (one long line). kledana: producing kleda (moistness). sarvarasapratyanīkabhūta: literally "become an opponent of all tastes"; the line does not say how. āhārayogin: literally "joined with food". "Not excessively heavy" is the literal sense of nātyarthaṃ guruḥ.

english: Thus these six tastes, used separately or in combination, properly and in due measure, are for the benefit of the world of embodied beings (adhyātmaloka); but used otherwise than this, they become harmful. The wise one should use them properly and in due measure, only for benefit.
notes: Prose passage typed as a verse unit (one long line). ekatvena: literally "by oneness", taken as "in combination" opposed to pṛthaktvena. adhyātmaloka: literally "the world pertaining to the self", taken as the world of embodied beings.
lines_deva: इत्येवमेते षड्रसाः पृथक्त्वेनैकत्वेन वा मात्रशः सम्यगुपयुज्यमाना उपकाराय भवन्त्यध्यात्मलोकस्य अपकारकराः पुनरतोऽन्यथा भवन्त्युपयुज्यमानाः तान् विद्वानुपकारार्थमेव मात्रशः सम्यगुपयोजयेदिति
lines_iast: ityevamete ṣaḍrasāḥ pṛthaktvenaikatvena vā mātraśaḥ samyagupayujyamānā upakārāya bhavantyadhyātmalokasya apakārakarāḥ punarato'nyathā bhavantyupayujyamānāḥ tān vidvānupakārārthameva mātraśaḥ samyagupayojayediti

hindi: और यहाँ (श्लोक) हैं: जो द्रव्य वीर्य से शीतल और रस तथा पाक दोनों में मधुर हो, जो उन दोनों में अम्ल और उष्ण हो, और जो द्रव्य उन दोनों में कटु हो,
english: And here there are: a substance that is cold in vīrya and sweet in taste and vipāka; one that is sour in both and hot; and a substance that is pungent in both,
notes: SENTENCE: the sentence continues into unit 46. Line 1 (bhavanti cātra) is the lead-in formula. Whether the pungent substance is also hot is not stated in the line; the translation does not add it.
lines_deva: तयोरम्लं यदुष्णं च यद्द्रव्यं कटुकं तयोः
lines_iast: tayoramlaṃ yaduṣṇaṃ ca yaddravyaṃ kaṭukaṃ tayoḥ

hindi: उनके गुणों का संग्रह रस के उपदेश से बताया जाना चाहिए; जो वीर्य और पाक में विपरीत नहीं हैं, उनका (गुणसंग्रह इसी प्रकार) बताया जाएगा।
english: for these, the summary of qualities is to be indicated by the teaching on taste; for those that are not contrary in vīrya and in vipāka, (the summary) will be taught (thus).
notes: SENTENCE: continues from unit 45. The second line is taken as restating the rule: the summary of qualities of substances whose vīrya and vipāka are not contrary to their taste is taught through the taste. upadekṣyate may also be read "it will be taught (later)"; the line does not decide.

hindi: जैसे दूध, जैसे घी, अथवा जैसे चव्य और चित्रक; ऐसे और अन्य द्रव्यों को वैद्य रस के आधार पर बताए।
english: As milk, as ghee, or as cavya and citraka: these and other such the physician should describe by their taste.
lines_deva: यथा पयो यथा सर्पिर्यथा वा चव्यचित्रकौ
lines_iast: yathā payo yathā sarpiryathā vā cavyacitrakau

words.gram: n. nom. sg., dvandva used as adjective of āmiṣam

hindi: कोई मधुर द्रव्य उष्ण हो सकता है, तथा कषाय और तिक्त भी; जैसे महत् पञ्चमूल, जैसे जल में उत्पन्न और आनूप (प्राणियों) का मांस।
english: Some sweet (substance) may be hot, and also the astringent and bitter; for example the great pañcamūla, or the flesh of water-born and marsh (animals).
notes: The line does not say which example belongs to which taste. madhuram is printed with final m before kiṃcit (not anusvāra), an orthographic variant only. No identifications of the animals.
lines_deva: मधुरम् किंचिदुष्णं स्यात् कषायं तिक्तमेव च
lines_iast: madhuram kiṃciduṣṇaṃ syāt kaṣāyaṃ tiktameva ca

hindi: लवण सैन्धव उष्ण नहीं है, उसी प्रकार अम्ल आमलक; तिक्त अर्क, अगुरु और गुडूची का (वीर्य) उष्ण कहा जाता है।
english: The salty saindhava is not hot, and likewise the sour āmalaka; of the bitter arka, aguru and guḍūcī, (the vīrya) is said to be hot.
notes: Plant identification: āmalaka = Phyllanthus emblica (standard). saindhava: literally "from Sindhu", a salt. "vīrya" is understood from the context of units 45-46.

hindi: कोई अम्ल द्रव्य संग्राही होता है और कोई अम्ल भेदन करता है; जैसे कपित्थ संग्राही है और आमलक भेदी।
english: Some sour (substance) is binding, and some sour (substance) breaks (purges): as kapittha is binding, and āmalaka likewise breaking (purgative).
notes: Plant identification: kapittha = wood-apple (standard). hi is left untranslated.
lines_deva: किंचिदम्लं हि संग्राहि किंचिदम्लं भिनत्ति च
यथा कपित्थं संग्राहि भेदि चामलकं तथा
lines_iast: kiṃcidamlaṃ hi saṃgrāhi kiṃcidamlaṃ bhinatti ca
yathā kapitthaṃ saṃgrāhi bhedi cāmalakaṃ tathā

hindi: पिप्पली और नागर वृष्य हैं, और कटु अवृष्य कहा जाता है; कषाय स्तम्भन और शीतल है, (पर) अभया में वह इससे भिन्न है।
english: Pippalī (long pepper) and nāgara (dry ginger) are aphrodisiac, and the pungent is said to be non-aphrodisiac; the astringent is checking and cold, (but) in abhayā it is otherwise than this.
notes: Plant identifications: pippalī = Piper longum (standard); abhayā = Terminalia chebula (standard). vṛṣyam is neuter singular, agreeing with the nearer word nāgaram. The contrast "(but)" is understood; the Sanskrit has no particle there.

hindi: इसलिए रस के उपदेश से सब द्रव्यों का निर्देश न करे; इस प्रकार समान रस वाले द्रव्य में भी प्रत्येक द्रव्य में गुण का भेद देखा जाता है।
english: Therefore one should not declare every substance by the teaching on taste; thus, even in a substance of equal taste, a difference of quality is seen in each substance.

text_flags.why: dravya is neuter, accusative dravyam (agreeing with sarvaṃ); dravyām is not a form; the metre also needs a short fifth syllable in this even quarter (dra-vya-mā-di-śet)
dental t after ṣ is not possible; the past participle of √dṛś is dṛṣṭa

hindi: रूक्षता के कारण रूक्ष रसों में कषाय उत्तम, कटु मध्यम और तिक्त अवर है; उसी प्रकार उष्ण रसों में उष्णता के कारण लवण सबसे बढ़कर है,
english: By dryness, among the dry (tastes) the astringent is highest, the pungent middle, the bitter lowest; likewise among the hot, by hotness the salty is highest,
notes: SENTENCE: the hot series continues into unit 54.

hindi: अम्ल मध्यम और कटु अन्तिम है; स्निग्ध रसों में मधुर सबसे बढ़कर, अम्ल मध्यम और लवण रस स्निग्धता के कारण अन्तिम कहा जाता है।
english: the sour middle, and the pungent last; among the unctuous, the sweet is highest, the sour middle, and the salty taste is declared last by unctuousness.

text_flags.why: possible: the passive of √vac is ucyate with short u (as printed ucyate in units 32 and 49); long ū is not a form

notes: SENTENCE: continues from unit 53.

hindi: शीतलता के कारण कषाय, मधुर और तिक्त क्रमशः मध्यम, उत्कृष्ट और अवर हैं; गुरुता के कारण मधुर सबसे अधिक है, और लवण कषाय से अवर है।
english: By coldness the astringent, sweet and bitter are respectively middle, highest and lowest; by heaviness the sweet is the greatest, and the salty is lower than the astringent.

text_flags.why: svadu is not a word; the first line of this unit prints svādu (sweet) in kaṣāyasvādutiktakāḥ

notes: The order "respectively" follows the order of the two compounds. For heaviness the astringent is implied as second (salty is lower than it); this is not printed. SENTENCE: the line kaṣāyāl lavaṇo 'varaḥ may run into unit 56.

hindi: लघुता के कारण अम्ल से कटु और उसके बाद तिक्त क्रमशः उत्तरोत्तर उत्तम हैं; कुछ लोग लघु रसों में लवण रस को अवर मानते हैं।
english: By lightness, the pungent (is above) the sour, and then the bitter, each higher in turn; some hold the salty taste to be the lowest among the light.
notes: amlāt is read as "than the sour" with kaṭuḥ (pungent above sour in lightness); another reading joins amlāt to the heaviness series of unit 55 (salty lower than astringent, and pungent lower than sour). The line does not decide. icchanti: literally "wish", here "hold (as their view)".

hindi: गुरुता तथा लघुता में, दोनों में भी वह निम्नतम है। और इसके बाद विपाकों का लक्षण कहा जाएगा।
english: In heaviness and in lightness, in both too, it is the lowest. And after this the characteristics of the vipākas (post-digestive effects) will be stated.

text_flags.why: possible: -styū- is not a sandhi form; tu + ubhayoḥ gives tūbhayoḥ (grammar), the y looks intrusive; same syllable count

notes: saḥ 'that (taste)' refers back to the taste named in the preceding verse, which lies outside this chunk. The split uses the suggested reading tu. saṃpravakṣyate is a middle future used in a passive sense ('will be stated').

words.gloss: of the pungent, bitter and astringent

hindi: कटु, तिक्त और कषाय (रसों) का विपाक प्रायः कटु होता है; अम्ल अम्ल रूप में पचता है, मधुर मधुर रूप में, और लवण उसी प्रकार।
english: The vipāka of the pungent, bitter and astringent (tastes) is mostly pungent; the sour is digested to sour, the sweet (svādu) to sweet, and the salt likewise.

text_flags.why: the genitive plural ending is -āṇām; -āṇaṃ is not a form (grammar); same syllable count

notes: tathā 'likewise' most naturally continues the last clause, i.e. the salt also is digested to sweet; the verse does not say so in a separate word. madhuram with final m before l is an orthographic variant of madhuraṃ, not flagged.

hindi: मधुर, तथा लवण और अम्ल — ये तीन रस स्निग्ध स्वभाव के कारण वायु, मूत्र और पुरीष के निकलने में प्रायः सुखकर माने गए हैं।
english: The sweet, and the salt and sour — these three tastes, because of their unctuous nature, are held to be mostly easy in the release of wind, urine and faeces.
notes: vāta here is the wind released from the body (with urine and faeces), not the doṣa.

words.gloss: of wind, faeces, urine and semen

hindi: परन्तु कटु, तिक्त और कषाय — ये तीन रस रूक्ष स्वभाव के कारण वायु, विष्ठा, मूत्र और शुक्र के निकलने में कष्टकारक देखे जाते हैं।
english: But the pungent, bitter and astringent — these three tastes, because of their dry nature, are seen to cause difficulty in the release of wind, faeces, urine and semen.
notes: vāta = wind released from the body, as in 59.

hindi: कटु विपाक शुक्र का नाशक, विष्ठा और मूत्र को बाँधने वाला तथा वात को बढ़ाने वाला है; मधुर विपाक विष्ठा और मूत्र को निकालने वाला तथा कफ और शुक्र को बढ़ाने वाला है।
english: The pungent vipāka destroys semen, binds faeces and urine and increases Vāta; the sweet vipāka lets faeces and urine pass and increases Kapha and semen.
notes: baddha-/sṛṣṭa-viṇmūtra: literally 'by which faeces and urine are bound / released'. vātala here describes the vipāka (Vāta-increasing), not a person.

hindi: अम्ल पाक पित्त उत्पन्न करने वाला, विष्ठा और मूत्र को निकालने वाला और शुक्र का नाशक है। इनमें मधुर गुरु होता है; कटु और अम्ल इससे भिन्न हैं।
english: The sour pāka produces Pitta, lets faeces and urine pass and destroys semen. Of these the sweet is heavy; the pungent and the sour are otherwise than this.
notes: pāka is used for vipāka. 'Otherwise than this' leaves the opposite (light) to be understood; the verse does not name it.

hindi: विपाक के लक्षण की अल्पता, मध्यमता और अधिकता के विषय में, द्रव्यों के गुणों की विशेषता से उस-उस (द्रव्य) में (उसे) पहचाने।
english: As for the small, medium or greatest degree of the characteristic of vipāka, one should observe (it) in each (substance) from the particular qualities of the substances.
notes: tatra tatra 'there and there' = in each case.

words.gloss: soft, sharp, heavy, light, unctuous, dry, hot, cold

hindi: कुछ (लोग) वीर्य को आठ प्रकार का — मृदु, तीक्ष्ण, गुरु, लघु, स्निग्ध, रूक्ष, उष्ण और शीतल — मानते आए हैं; कुछ दो प्रकार का —
english: Some have held vīrya (potency) to be eightfold: soft, sharp, heavy, light, unctuous, dry, hot and cold; some, twofold —
notes: SENTENCE: 'some, twofold' is completed by śītoṣṇam iti in 65. āsthitāḥ serves both kecit.

hindi: — शीत और उष्ण। वीर्य तो वह है जिससे जो क्रिया की जाती है; वीर्यहीन कुछ नहीं करता; सारी क्रिया वीर्य से की हुई होती है।
english: — (namely) cold and hot. Vīrya, indeed, is that by which an action, whatever it is, is done; what lacks vīrya does nothing; all action is done by vīrya.
notes: SENTENCE: śītoṣṇam iti completes 'some, twofold' of 64.
lines_deva: शीतोष्णमिति वीर्यं तु क्रियते येन या क्रिया
नावीर्यं कुरुते किंचित् सर्वा वीर्यकृता क्रिया
lines_iast: śītoṣṇamiti vīryaṃ tu kriyate yena yā kriyā
nāvīryaṃ kurute kiṃcit sarvā vīryakṛtā kriyā

words.gloss: by the final outcome of action

hindi: द्रव्यों का रस संपर्क होने पर, विपाक कर्म की परिणति से, और वीर्य संपर्क से तथा जब तक (द्रव्य) ठहरता है तब तक जाना जाता है।
english: The taste (rasa) of substances is perceived on contact, the vipāka by the final outcome of (their) action, and vīrya from contact and for as long as (the substance) stays.
notes: upalabhyate serves all three clauses. yāvadadhīvāsāt is read as yāvat + adhīvāsāt 'as long as (it) stays'; where it stays is not stated. nipāta, literally 'falling upon', = contact.

hindi: जहाँ रस, वीर्य और विपाक की समानता दिखती है और कर्मों में विशेषता ही (दिखती है), वह उसका प्रभाव कहा गया है।
english: Where sameness (sāmānya) of rasa, vīrya and vipāka is observed, and indeed a difference (viśeṣa) in actions, that is known as its prabhāva (specific potency).
notes: tasya 'of it' = of the substance.
lines_deva: विशेषः कर्मणां चैव प्रभावस्तस्य स स्मृतः
lines_iast: viśeṣaḥ karmaṇāṃ caiva prabhāvastasya sa smṛtaḥ

hindi: चित्रक (रस में) कटु, पाक में कटु और वीर्य में उष्ण माना गया है; दन्ती उसी के समान है, परन्तु प्रभाव से वह मनुष्य का विरेचन करती है।
english: Citraka is held to be pungent (in taste), pungent in pāka and hot in vīrya; dantī is like it, but by prabhāva it purges a man.
notes: citraka and dantī kept Sanskrit.

words.gram: n. nom. sg., derivative (-ika) of the dvandva ūrdhva-anuloma
n. nom. sg., tat-puruṣa, ppp. caus. pra-√bhū

hindi: जो विष विषनाशक कहा गया है, वहाँ प्रभाव कारण है; और जो ऊर्ध्व तथा अनुलोम कार्य करने वाला है, वह प्रभाव से उत्पन्न है।
english: The poison that is said to destroy poison — prabhāva is the cause there; and that which acts upward and downward (ūrdhvānulomika) is brought about by prabhāva.
notes: ūrdhvānulomika: literally 'upward and in the downward direction (anuloma)'; whether one substance is meant to act both ways is not stated.

words.gram: n. nom. sg., tat-puruṣa, ppp. ā-√kṛ

hindi: धारण करने योग्य मणियों का जो विविध प्रकार का कर्म है, वह उनके प्रभाव से किया हुआ है; प्रभाव अचिन्त्य कहा जाता है।
english: The action of gems that are to be worn, which is of various kinds, is effected by their prabhāva; prabhāva is called inconceivable.
notes: prabhāvākṛtaṃ is split as prabhāva + ākṛta 'effected'; a compound prabhāvakṛta (cf. vīryakṛtā in 65) would give the same sense, so the printed long ā is kept without a flag.

hindi: विपाक और वीर्य भली-भाँति कह दिए गए, और प्रभाव भी बताया गया। (द्रव्य) कोई कर्म रस से करता है और दूसरा वीर्य से,
english: The vipākas and vīryas have been properly stated, and prabhāva also has been stated. (A substance) does some action by taste and another by vīrya,
notes: SENTENCE: kurute karma runs into 72 (dravyaṃ ... kiṃcana). udāhṛtaḥ agrees with prabhāvaḥ; the same verb is understood for vipākavīryāṇi.

hindi: द्रव्य कोई (कर्म) गुण से, पाक से और प्रभाव से करता है। रस को विपाक दबा देता है, उन दोनों को वीर्य, और उन (तीनों) को प्रभाव —
english: the substance (does) some by quality, by pāka and by prabhāva. Vipāka overrides taste, vīrya those two, and prabhāva those (three) —
notes: SENTENCE: line 1 completes 71b; line 2 is completed by balasāmye in 73. apohati 'removes, overrides' is the one verb of all three clauses; vīryaṃ is the neuter nominative subject of the second.
lines_deva: द्रव्यं गुणेन पाकेन प्रभावेण च किंचन
lines_iast: dravyaṃ guṇena pākena prabhāveṇa ca kiṃcana

hindi: — जब रस आदि का बल समान हो। यह (उनका) स्वाभाविक बल है। इसके आगे मैं छह रसों की पहचान का उपदेश करूँगा।
english: — when the strength of rasa and the rest is equal: this is (their) natural strength. From here onward I shall teach the recognition of the six tastes.
notes: SENTENCE: balasāmye completes 72b. vijñāna here = recognition (how each taste is known), as the following verses show.

words.gloss: by oleating, pleasing, delighting and softening

words.gram: m. nom. sg., pres. part. vi-√āp

hindi: मधुर (रस) स्नेहन, प्रीणन, आह्लाद और मृदुता से पहचाना जाता है; और मुख में स्थित होकर वह मुख में व्याप्त होता हुआ मानो उसे लीप देता है।
english: The sweet is recognised by oleating (snehana), pleasing, delighting and softening; and staying in the mouth, the sweet, pervading the mouth, as it were coats it.
notes: The subject madhuraḥ stands in line 2 but serves both lines.

words.gloss: from setting the teeth on edge

hindi: दाँतों की सिहरन, मुख से स्राव, स्वेदन, मुख के जागरण और मुख तथा कण्ठ की जलन से, चखकर ही (उसे) अम्ल रस कहे।
english: From the setting of the teeth on edge, salivation, sweating, awakening of the mouth and burning of the mouth and throat, one should, just on tasting (it), declare (it) the sour taste.
notes: mukhāsrāva, literally 'flow from the mouth', = salivation.

words.gram: m. nom. sg., pres. part. pra-√lī

hindi: जो घुलता हुआ मुख में शीघ्र क्लेद, विष्यन्द और मृदुता उत्पन्न करता है, और मुख की जलन से (पहचाना जाता है), वह लवण जानना चाहिए।
english: That which, dissolving, quickly produces moistness (kleda), liquefaction (viṣyanda) and softness in the mouth, and (is known) from the burning of the mouth, is to be known as the salt.
notes: śīghram may go with pralīyan ('dissolving quickly') or with kurute; the sense is the same.
lines_deva: यः शीघ्रं लवणो ज्ञेयः स विदाहान्मुखस्य च
lines_iast: yaḥ śīghraṃ lavaṇo jñeyaḥ sa vidāhānmukhasya ca

words.gram: m. nom. sg., pres. part. vi-√dah

hindi: रसों में से जो संपर्क होने पर उत्तेजित करता है और मानो चुभता है, तथा मुख, नाक और आँखों को जलाता हुआ स्राव कराता है, वह कटु कहा गया है।
english: That one among the tastes which, on contact, excites and as it were pricks, and, burning the mouth, nose and eyes, causes discharge, is known as the pungent.
notes: rasānāṃ is read as a partitive genitive ('among the tastes'); saṃvejayet then has no expressed object. Reading rasanāṃ 'the tongue' (cf. rasanaṃ in 78 and 79) would give it one; not adopted, since the printed form gives sense.

words.gloss: producing non-sliminess of the mouth, dryness and gladdening

hindi: जो संपर्क होने पर रसना को प्रतिहत करता है और रुचिकर नहीं लगता, वह तिक्त है; वह मुख में विशदता, शोष और प्रह्लाद उत्पन्न करता है।
english: That which on contact repels the tongue and is not pleasant (to it) is the bitter; it produces non-sliminess (vaiśadya) of the mouth, dryness and gladdening (prahlāda).
notes: rasanam (n.) = the tongue.
lines_deva: प्रतिहन्ति निपाते यो रसनं स्वदते न च
lines_iast: pratihanti nipāte yo rasanaṃ svadate na ca

hindi: जो रस रसना को विशदता, स्तम्भ और जड़ता से युक्त करता है और जो मानो कण्ठ को बाँध देता है, वह कषाय है; वह विकासी भी है।
english: The taste which affects the tongue with non-sliminess, stiffness and numbness, and which as it were binds the throat, is the astringent; it is also vikāsin (expanding).
notes: vikāsin, literally 'opening, expanding'; its exact sense here is not explained in the verse.
lines_deva: बध्नातीव च यः कण्ठं कषायः स विकास्यपि
lines_iast: badhnātīva ca yaḥ kaṇṭhaṃ kaṣāyaḥ sa vikāsyapi

words.gloss: on the topic of substances, qualities and actions

words.gram: n. acc. sg., pres. pass. part. upa-√diś

hindi: ऐसा कह चुके भगवान् आत्रेय से अग्निवेश ने कहा — भगवन्, द्रव्य, गुण और कर्म के विषय में आप भगवान् का यथावत् कहा गया यह सत्य और अर्थ-सम्पत् से युक्त वचन सुन लिया गया; परन्तु आगे हम वैरोधिक आहार-विकारों का लक्षण अति संक्षेप के बिना उपदेश किया जाता हुआ सुनना चाहते हैं।
english: To the venerable Ātreya, who had spoken thus, Agniveśa said: 'Venerable one, this true speech of the venerable one, endowed with excellence of meaning, (given) properly on the topic of substances, qualities and actions, has been heard. But next we wish to hear the characteristics of the incompatible (vairodhika) food articles (āhāravikāra) taught not too briefly.'
notes: Prose passage typed as a verse unit (type 'verse', one long line). bhagavataḥ 'of the venerable one' is respectful address in the third person. āhāravikāra, literally 'modifications of food', = food articles.
lines_deva: एवमुक्तवन्तं भगवन्तमात्रेयमग्निवेश उवाच भगवन् श्रुतमेतदवितथमर्थसंपद्युक्तं भगवतो यथावद्द्रव्यगुणकर्माधिकारे वचः परं त्वाहारविकाराणां वैरोधिकानां लक्षणमनतिसंक्षेपेणोपदिश्यमानं शुश्रूषामह इति
lines_iast: evamuktavantaṃ bhagavantamātreyamagniveśa uvāca bhagavan śrutametadavitathamarthasaṃpadyuktaṃ bhagavato yathāvaddravyaguṇakarmādhikāre vacaḥ paraṃ tvāhāravikārāṇāṃ vairodhikānāṃ lakṣaṇamanatisaṃkṣepeṇopadiśyamānaṃ śuśrūṣāmaha iti

words.gloss: by place, time, measure and the like

hindi: भगवान् आत्रेय ने उससे कहा — शरीर की धातुओं के प्रतिकूल द्रव्य शरीर की धातुओं से विरोध को प्राप्त होते हैं; कुछ परस्पर गुणों से विरुद्ध होते हैं, कुछ संयोग से, दूसरे संस्कार से, और दूसरे देश, काल, मात्रा आदि से, तथा दूसरे स्वभाव से।
english: The venerable Ātreya said to him: Substances that are opposed to the body-dhātus enter into conflict with the body-dhātus: some are opposed through their mutual qualities, some through combination, others through processing, and others by place, time, measure and the like, and likewise others by their own nature.
notes: Prose passage typed as a verse unit. The first kānicit goes with parasparaguṇaviruddhāni, the second with saṃyogāt; 'opposed' is understood with the later items.
lines_deva: तमुवाच भगवानात्रेयः देहधातुप्रत्यनीकभूतानि द्रव्याणि देहधातुभिर्विरोधमापद्यन्ते परस्परगुणविरुद्धानि कानिचित् कानिचित् संयोगात् संस्कारादपराणि देशकालमात्रादिभिश्चापराणि तथा स्वभावादपराणि
lines_iast: tamuvāca bhagavānātreyaḥ dehadhātupratyanīkabhūtāni dravyāṇi dehadhātubhirvirodhamāpadyante parasparaguṇaviruddhāni kānicit kānicit saṃyogāt saṃskārādaparāṇi deśakālamātrādibhiścāparāṇi tathā svabhāvādaparāṇi

words.gloss: because of being cold and hot
because of being opposed in vīrya

hindi: उनमें से जो (द्रव्य) आहार के रूप में सबसे अधिक उपयोग में आते हैं, उनमें से वैरोधिक के विषय में एक अंश का हम उपदेश करेंगे। मछलियों को दूध के साथ न खाए; क्योंकि ये दोनों मधुर, मधुर विपाक वाले और अत्यन्त अभिष्यन्दी हैं; शीत और उष्ण होने से विरुद्ध वीर्य वाले हैं; विरुद्ध वीर्य होने से रक्त को दूषित करने के लिए और अत्यन्त अभिष्यन्दी होने से मार्गों के अवरोध के लिए (होते हैं)।
english: Among these, of the (substances) which are used most with reference to food, we shall teach a part, with reference to the incompatible. One should not eat fish together with milk. For both of these are sweet, sweet in vipāka and greatly channel-clogging (abhiṣyandin); because of being cold and hot they are opposed in vīrya; because of being opposed in vīrya they lead to vitiation of the blood, and because of being greatly channel-clogging, to obstruction of the passages (mārga).
notes: Prose passage typed as a verse unit. The passage does not say which of the two is cold and which hot. ubhayam (n. sg.) 'both' takes neuter singular predicates. viruddhavīryā = viruddhavīryāḥ (m. nom. pl., visarga dropped before v): the two things (fish and milk) are construed as a plural; the printed form is kept, no flag.
lines_deva: तत्र यान्याहारमधिकृत्य भूयिष्ठमुपयुज्यन्ते तेषामेकदेशं वैरोधिकमधिकृत्योपदेक्ष्यामः न मत्स्यान् पयसा सहाभ्यवहरेत् उभयं ह्येतन्मधुरं मधुरविपाकं महाभिष्यन्दि शीतोष्णत्वाद्विरुद्धवीर्या विरुद्धवीर्यत्वाच्छोणितप्रदूषणाय महाभिष्यन्दित्वान्मार्गोपरोधाय च
lines_iast: tatra yānyāhāramadhikṛtya bhūyiṣṭhamupayujyante teṣāmekadeśaṃ vairodhikamadhikṛtyopadekṣyāmaḥ na matsyān payasā sahābhyavaharet ubhayaṃ hyetanmadhuraṃ madhuravipākaṃ mahābhiṣyandi śītoṣṇatvādviruddhavīryā viruddhavīryatvācchoṇitapradūṣaṇāya mahābhiṣyanditvānmārgoparodhāya ca

hindi: आत्रेय के उस वचन को सुनकर, फिर भद्रकाप्य ने अग्निवेश से कहा — सभी मछलियों को दूध के साथ खाए, एक चिलिचिम को छोड़कर। वह फिर शल्कों वाला, लाल आँखों वाला, सब ओर लाल धारियों वाला और रोहित के आकार का होता है, और प्रायः भूमि पर विचरता है। यदि उसे दूध के साथ खाए तो निःसन्देह रक्त से उत्पन्न और विबन्ध से उत्पन्न रोगों में से कोई एक, अथवा मृत्यु प्राप्त करे।
english: Having heard that statement of Ātreya, Bhadrakāpya then said to Agniveśa: 'One may eat all fish indeed with milk, except the one cilicima. That one, moreover, is scaly, red-eyed, with red streaks all over and shaped like the rohita, and it mostly moves on the ground. If one eats it with milk, one would without doubt get one of the diseases born of blood and of obstruction, or death.'
notes: Prose passage typed as a verse unit. cilicima and rohita are fish names kept Sanskrit, no identification. śakalin = having scales (śakala). abhyavaharet in the first sentence is a permissive optative ('one may eat').
lines_deva: तन्निशम्यात्रेयवचनमनु भद्रकाप्योऽग्निवेशमुवाच सर्वानेव मत्स्यान् पयसा सहाभ्यवहरेदन्यत्रैकस्माच्चिलिचिमात् स पुनः शकली लोहितनयनः सर्वतो लोहितराजी रोहिताकारः प्रायो भूमौ चरति तं चेत् पयसा सहाभ्यवहरेन्निःसंशयं शोणितजानां विबन्धजानां च व्याधीनामन्यतममथवा मरणं प्राप्नुयादिति
lines_iast: tanniśamyātreyavacanamanu bhadrakāpyo'gniveśamuvāca sarvāneva matsyān payasā sahābhyavaharedanyatraikasmāccilicimāt sa punaḥ śakalī lohitanayanaḥ sarvato lohitarājī rohitākāraḥ prāyo bhūmau carati taṃ cet payasā sahābhyavaharenniḥsaṃśayaṃ śoṇitajānāṃ vibandhajānāṃ ca vyādhīnāmanyatamamathavā maraṇaṃ prāpnuyāditi

hindi: भगवान् आत्रेय ने कहा — नहीं; सभी मछलियों को दूध के साथ न खाए, विशेषकर चिलिचिम को; क्योंकि वह अत्यन्त अभिष्यन्दी होने से इन रोगों को अधिक स्थूल लक्षणों वाला उत्पन्न करता है और आमविष को उभारता है।
english: 'No,' said the venerable Ātreya; 'one should not eat any fish at all with milk, but especially not the cilicima; for it, because of being greatly channel-clogging, produces these diseases with grosser signs and stirs up āmaviṣa (poison of undigested matter).'

text_flags.why: word division misplaced: Ātreya's 'no' (neti) answers Bhadrakāpya's 'sarvāneva matsyān payasā sahābhyavaharet' (83), so the negative na is needed; it is printed as -n + a- of the next word, and apayasā 'without milk' gives no sense with saha

notes: Prose passage typed as a verse unit. The split gives na to the token matsyānn and payasā to apayasā, following the suggested word division. 'these diseases' = those named by Bhadrakāpya in 83. The printed -ānn before a vowel is itself no possible sandhi (n is doubled only after a short vowel), which supports the re-division matsyān na payasā.
lines_deva: नेति भगवानात्रेयः सर्वानेव मत्स्यान्न् अपयसा सहाभ्यवहरेद्विशेषतस्तु चिलिचिमं स हि महाभिष्यन्दित्वात् स्थूललक्षणतरानेतान् व्याधीनुपजनयत्यामविषमुदीरयति च
lines_iast: neti bhagavānātreyaḥ sarvāneva matsyānn apayasā sahābhyavaharedviśeṣatastu cilicimaṃ sa hi mahābhiṣyanditvāt sthūlalakṣaṇatarānetān vyādhīnupajanayatyāmaviṣamudīrayati ca

words.gloss: meats of domestic, marsh and aquatic (animals)
with honey, sesame, jaggery, milk, māṣa, mūlaka, lotus stalk
deafness, blindness, tremor, torpor, indistinct speech, dumbness, nasal speech

hindi: और ग्राम्य, आनूप और औदक (पशुओं) के मांस को मधु, तिल, गुड़, दूध, माष, मूलक, बिस अथवा अंकुरित धान्यों के साथ एक साथ न खाए; क्योंकि उसके कारण (मनुष्य) बहरापन, अन्धापन, कम्पन, जड़ता, अस्पष्ट वाणी, गूँगापन, मिनमिनाकर बोलना अथवा मृत्यु प्राप्त करता है।
english: And one should not eat the meats of domestic, marsh and aquatic (animals) together with honey, sesame, jaggery, milk, māṣa, mūlaka, lotus stalk or sprouted grains; for, caused by that, one gets deafness, blindness, tremor, torpor (jāḍya), indistinct speech (kala), dumbness, nasal speech (maiṇmiṇya), or death.

text_flags.why: possible: kaṣisa is not a word; bisa (lotus stalk) gives a food item fitting the list, and printed ष and ब are easily confused in Devanagari

notes: māṣa = black gram; mūlaka = radish. kala-mūkatā: -tā is read over kala-mūka ('indistinctness of speech and dumbness'); it may also be one item ('inarticulate dumbness'); uncertain. maiṇmiṇya is one word (aiṇmiṇya would be none), so mūkatā stays inside the compound. maiṇmiṇya = speaking through the nose. The subject of āpnoti (the eater) is understood.
lines_deva: ग्राम्यानूपौदकपिशितानि च मधुतिलगुडपयोमाषमूलकषिसैर्विरूढधान्यैर्वा नैकध्यमद्यात् तन्मूलं हि बाधिर्यान्ध्यवेपथुजाड्यकलमूकतामैण्मिण्यमथवा मरणमाप्नोति

words.gloss: of clogging of blood, accumulation in the vessels, apasmāra, śaṅkhaka, galagaṇḍa, rohiṇī

hindi: पौष्कर या रोहिणीक शाक को, अथवा सरसों के तेल में भुने कबूतरों को मधु और दूध के साथ न खाए; क्योंकि उसके कारण (मनुष्य) रक्त का अभिष्यन्द, धमनी-प्रविचय, अपस्मार, शङ्खक, गलगण्ड और रोहिणी में से कोई एक, अथवा मृत्यु प्राप्त करता है।
english: One should not eat the pauṣkara or rohiṇīka vegetable, or pigeons fried in mustard oil, together with honey and milk; for, caused by that, one gets one of these: clogging of the blood (śoṇitābhiṣyanda), accumulation in the vessels (dhamanīpravicaya), apasmāra, śaṅkhaka, galagaṇḍa and rohiṇī, or death.

text_flags.why: possible: bhraṣṭa (√bhraṃś) means 'fallen'; 'fried' is bhṛṣṭa (√bhrasj), as in sarṣapatailabhṛṣṭo (P25) and paribhṛṣṭā (P28) in this chunk

notes: pauṣkara and rohiṇīka are vegetable names kept Sanskrit, unidentified; the line does not say whether śākam goes with both. śoṇitābhiṣyanda may also be read as two items (śoṇita, abhiṣyanda); read as one. apasmāra, śaṅkhaka, galagaṇḍa, rohiṇī kept Sanskrit. The gender of the dvandva follows its last member rohiṇī (f.).
lines_deva: न पौष्करं रोहिणीकं शाकं कपोतान् वा सर्षपतैलभ्रष्टान्मधुपयोभ्यां सहाभ्यवहरेत् तन्मूलं हि शोणिताभिष्यन्दधमनीप्रविचयापस्मारशङ्खकगलगण्डरोहिणीनामन्यतमं प्राप्नोत्यथवा मरणमिति

words.gloss: mūlaka, laśuna, kṛṣṇagandhā, arjaka, sumukha, surasa and the like
for fear of affliction by kuṣṭha

hindi: मूलक, लशुन, कृष्णगन्धा, अर्जक, सुमुख, सुरस आदि खाकर दूध का सेवन नहीं करना चाहिए, कुष्ठ की बाधा के भय से।
english: Having eaten mūlaka, laśuna, kṛṣṇagandhā, arjaka, sumukha, surasa and the like, one should not take milk, for fear of affliction by kuṣṭha.
notes: laśuna = garlic; mūlaka = radish. surasa is the printed form, possibly surasā with the feminine shortened in a name inside the compound; kept as printed. The other names are kept Sanskrit.

hindi: न जातुक शाक और न पका हुआ निकुच मधु और दूध के साथ उपयोग करना चाहिए; क्योंकि यह मृत्यु के लिए, अथवा बल, वर्ण, तेज और वीर्य के अवरोध के लिए, गम्भीर रोग के लिए और नपुंसकता के लिए होता है।
english: Neither the jātuka vegetable nor ripe nikuca should be taken together with honey and milk; for this leads to death, or to obstruction of strength, complexion, lustre and virility (vīrya), to serious disease, and to impotence.
notes: vīrya here is the person's virility, not the potency of a drug. alaghu, literally 'not light', = serious. jātuka and nikuca kept Sanskrit; ṣāṇḍhya printed spelling kept.

english: That same ripe nikuca should not be taken with māṣa soup, jaggery and ghee, because of incompatibility. Likewise āmra, āmrātaka, mātuluṅga, nikuca, karamarda, moca, dantaśaṭha, badara, kośāmra, bhavya, jāmbava, kapittha, tintiḍīka, pārāvata, akṣoḍa, panasa, nālikera, dāḍima and āmalaka, and other substances of this kind, and everything sour, liquid or non-liquid, is incompatible with milk.
notes: The '|' attached to tathā is the edition's danda inside the line; it is left out of w. Nineteen items are named. māṣasūpa is read as one item (soup of māṣa); it could also be two (māṣa, sūpa). english: Likewise kaṅgu, vanaka, makuṣṭhaka, kulattha, māṣa and niṣyāva are incompatible with milk.
notes: Grain and pulse names kept Sanskrit. The reading vanaka is uncertain to the drafter as a grain name, but nothing in the chunk supports a correction, so no flag.

hindi: पद्मोत्तरिका शाक, शार्कर, मैरेय और मधु एक साथ उपयोग किए जाने पर विरुद्ध हैं और वात को अत्यधिक कुपित करते हैं।
english: The padmottarikā vegetable, śārkara, maireya and honey, used together, are incompatible and greatly aggravate Vāta.
notes: The predicates are singular (upayuktaṃ viruddhaṃ, atikopayati): the combination is meant. śārkara, literally 'made of sugar (śarkarā)', a liquor; maireya kept Sanskrit.
lines_deva: पद्मोत्तरिकाशाकं शार्करो मैरेयो मधु च सहोपयुक्तं विरुद्धं वातं चातिकोपयति
lines_iast: padmottarikāśākaṃ śārkaro maireyo madhu ca sahopayuktaṃ viruddhaṃ vātaṃ cātikopayati

hindi: सरसों के तेल में भुना हुआ हारिद्रक विरुद्ध है और पित्त को अत्यधिक कुपित करता है।
english: Hāridraka fried in mustard oil is incompatible and greatly aggravates Pitta.
notes: hāridraka kept Sanskrit; what it is, is not stated in this line.

hindi: मन्थ के अनुपान वाला पायस विरुद्ध है और श्लेष्मा को अत्यधिक कुपित करता है।
english: Milk-rice (pāyasa) with mantha as the after-drink is incompatible and greatly aggravates Kapha (śleṣman).

hindi: तिल के कल्क से सिद्ध की गई उपोदिका अतीसार का कारण है।
english: Upodikā cooked with sesame paste is a cause of diarrhoea (atīsāra).
notes: upodikā kept Sanskrit. atīsāra is the printed spelling (atisāra).

hindi: बलाका वारुणी के साथ, और कुल्माषों के साथ भी, विरुद्ध है; वही सूअर की वसा में भुनी हुई तुरन्त मार डालती है।
english: The balākā is incompatible with vāruṇī, and also with kulmāṣa; that same (balākā), fried in pig's muscle-fat, kills at once.
notes: balākā, vāruṇī and kulmāṣa kept Sanskrit, no identification. Whether vāruṇī and kulmāṣa are incompatible with the balākā separately or together is not stated.
lines_deva: बलाका वारुण्या सह कुल्माषैरपि विरुद्धा सैव शूकरवसापरिभृष्टा सद्यो व्यापादयति
lines_iast: balākā vāruṇyā saha kulmāṣairapi viruddhā saiva śūkaravasāparibhṛṣṭā sadyo vyāpādayati

english: Peacock meat fixed on a castor (eraṇḍa) sīsaka, scorched on a castor fire and combined with castor oil, kills at once.

words.gloss: prepared in the frying of fish

hindi: मत्स्य-निस्तालन में सिद्ध की गई पिप्पलियाँ, तथा काकमाची और मधु (साथ में) मृत्यु के लिए होते हैं।
english: Long peppers (pippalī) prepared in the frying of fish (matsyanistālana), and likewise kākamācī and honey (together), lead to death.
notes: nistālana is taken as 'frying' from the context of cooking; the medium (the oil or the pan used for the fish) is not stated, and the word's exact sense is uncertain. Whether kākamācī and honey are meant together (as a combination) or each separately is not explicit; the combination reading fits the list of incompatible pairs. pippalī = Piper longum (standard). Prose line.

hindi: और उष्ण मधु, और उष्णता से पीड़ित व्यक्ति के लिए मधु, मृत्यु के लिए होता है।
english: Hot honey, and honey for one afflicted by heat, lead to death.
notes: The opening ca links this line to the preceding list. Prose line.

words.gloss: roasted on a spit over charcoal

hindi: समान मात्रा में मधु और घी; मधु और आन्तरिक्ष जल समान मात्रा में; मधु और पुष्कर-बीज; मधु पीकर उष्ण जल; भल्लातक और उष्ण जल; तक्र में सिद्ध कम्पिल्लक; बासी काकमाची; और अङ्गारों पर सलाख पर भुना भास — ये विरुद्ध हैं।
english: Honey and ghee in equal measure; honey and rain-water in equal measure; honey and lotus seed (puṣkarabīja); hot water after drinking honey; bhallātaka with hot water; kampillaka prepared in buttermilk; stale kākamācī; and bhāsa roasted on a spit over charcoal: these are incompatible.
notes: vāri āntarikṣam = rain-water (water from the sky). bhāsa is an animal whose meat is meant (roasted on a spit); left unidentified. bhallātakoṣṇodakam is split as one samāhāra unit 'bhallātaka with hot water' by analogy with the pairs before it. Prose line.

english: Thus this has been set out according to the question.

english: And here there are: Whatever kind of food sets a doṣa flowing but does not remove it from the body, all that turns out to be harmful.
notes: āsrāvya (causative of ā-√sru) is taken literally as 'having set flowing', i.e. having stirred the doṣa from its place.

english: And that also which (is incompatible) by place, time, digestive fire, measure, suitability (sātmya), Vāta (anila) and the rest, by processing and by potency (vīrya), and also by bowel (koṣṭha), state and sequence,
notes: SENTENCE: 86 and 87 form one sentence; the main clause 'viruddhaṃ tac ca na hitam' is in 87. anila-ādi = Vāta and the other doṣas.

english: by restriction (parihāra) and manner of use (upacāra), by cooking and also by combination — that is incompatible and not wholesome, and (so is) what (is incompatible) by heart (hṛd), excellence (sampad) and rule (vidhi).

COUNT: the list in 86-87 names eighteen kinds (place, time, agni, measure, sātmya, the doṣas, processing, potency, bowel, state, sequence, restriction, upacāra, cooking, combination, heart, excellence, rule). The definitions that follow (88-101) take them in this order, but upacāra has no separately named definition in this chunk; the second half of 98 (cold after ghee) may be meant for it. 'hṛtsaṃpadvidhibhiḥ' is grammatically gender-mixed; m. given for the plural compound.

english: Incompatible by time also is the use of cold, dry and similar things in the cold season, and likewise the use of pungent, hot and similar things in the hot (season).

hindi: इसी प्रकार चार प्रकार के अनल से विरुद्ध अन्न-पान (होता है)। समान मात्रा में मधु और घी — वह मात्रा से विरुद्ध होता है।
english: Likewise, (there is) food and drink incompatible with the fourfold digestive fire (anala). Honey and ghee in equal measure: that is incompatible by measure.
notes: The locative anale is taken as 'with regard to the digestive fire'; the four kinds of fire are not named in this chunk.

use of sweet, cold and the like

hindi: कटु, उष्ण आदि जिसके लिए सात्म्य हों, उसके द्वारा मधुर, शीत आदि का जो सेवन है, वह सात्म्य-विरुद्ध है; और अनिल आदि से विरुद्ध —
english: For one to whom pungent, hot and similar things are suitable (sātmya), the use of sweet, cold and similar things: that is incompatible with suitability. And incompatible with Vāta (anila) and the rest
notes: SENTENCE: the last clause (incompatible with Vāta and the rest) is completed by 92a.

words.gloss: use of food and herbs incompatible through habitual use of the same qualities

hindi: (वह है) जो (अनिल आदि के) समान गुणों के अभ्यास से विरुद्ध अन्न और औषधि का प्रयोग है। संस्कार से विरुद्ध वह है, जो भोज्य विष के समान हो जाए —
english: is the use of food and herbs that is incompatible through habitual use of the same qualities (as Vāta and the rest). Incompatible by processing is that food which would become like poison,
notes: SENTENCE: 92a completes 91b; 92b runs on into 93a. The long compound is ambiguous: it may also be read as 'the use of food and medicine of the same qualities (as Vāta etc.), and incompatible (made so) by habitual use'. auṣadhi (herb) is kept as printed beside the more usual auṣadha (medicine); the sense is the same here.

english: is taken combined with a substance of hot potency. And for one with a hard bowel (krūrakoṣṭha), (what is) very little, of mild potency and non-purgative,

words.gloss: for one with a soft bowel

words.gram: n. nom. sg., gerundive (kṛtya) √bhid, used as adj.

hindi: और मृदु कोष्ठ वाले के लिए गुरु, भेदक तथा अधिक — यह कोष्ठ-विरुद्ध है; और अवस्था से विरुद्ध होगा —
english: and for one with a soft bowel (mṛdukoṣṭha), (what is) heavy, purgative and likewise much: this is incompatible with the bowel (koṣṭha). And incompatible by state (avasthā) would be
notes: SENTENCE: the last clause is completed by 96.
lines_deva: मृदुकोष्ठस्य गुरु च भेदनीयं तथा बहु
lines_iast: mṛdukoṣṭhasya guru ca bhedanīyaṃ tathā bahu

words.gloss: for one engaged in exertion, sexual intercourse and exercise
words.gram: m. gen. sg., tat-puruṣa (dvandva first member)

hindi: श्रम, व्यवाय और व्यायाम में लगे हुए व्यक्ति के लिए अनिल को कुपित करने वाला (भोजन), और निद्रा से अलसाए आलसी व्यक्ति के लिए श्लेष्मा को कुपित करने वाला भोजन।
english: food aggravating Vāta (anila) for one engaged in exertion (śrama), sexual intercourse (vyavāya) and exercise, and food aggravating Kapha (śleṣman) for one who is languid with sleep and lazy.
notes: SENTENCE: completes 95b. bhojanam is understood with anilakopanam too. nidrālasasya and alasasya are taken as two genitives describing one person.

words.gloss: (one) under the sway of excessive hunger

hindi: और जो मल-मूत्र का त्याग किए बिना खाता है, और जो भूख न होने पर खाता है, वह क्रम-विरुद्ध होता है; और जो अत्यधिक भूख के वश में होकर (खाता है)।
english: And when one eats without voiding faeces and urine, and one who eats when not hungry: that would be incompatible by sequence (krama); and (so is it) when one (eats) under the sway of excessive hunger.
notes: The construction is loose: yat (n.) is paired with the masculine yaḥ and ...anugaḥ (the eater); 'one who eats' is understood in each clause. viṭ-mūtra is a samāhāra dvandva (neuter singular), as printed in one compound.

hindi: परिहार से विरुद्ध वह है, जब कोई सूअर आदि का सेवन करके उष्ण का सेवन करे; और घी आदि पीकर शीतल का सेवन करता है।
english: And incompatible by restriction (parihāra) is when, having eaten boar and the like, one takes something hot, and (when), having drunk ghee and the like, one takes something cold.
notes: The second clause (cold after ghee) is joined to parihāra by ca as printed; it may be the example meant for upacāra, which is listed in 87 but not separately named in this chunk.

words.gram: n. nom. sg., tat-puruṣa, ppp. caus. √sādh

words.gloss: with rice left raw, overcooked or burnt
words.gram: n. nom. sg., bahuvrīhi / dvandva of adjectives

hindi: पाक से भी विरुद्ध वह है जो दूषित और बुरे ईंधन-काष्ठ से पकाया गया हो, और जो कच्चे चावल वाला, अत्यधिक पका हुआ या जला हुआ हो; संयोग से विरुद्ध वह है, जैसे दूध के साथ अम्ल।
english: Incompatible by cooking also is what is prepared with spoiled, bad fuel-wood, and what is (cooked) with the rice left raw, overcooked or burnt; incompatible by combination is, for example, something sour with milk.

text_flags.why: possible: the feminine ending -ā has nothing to agree with; yat and viruddham in the same verse are neuter

notes: The compound in 99b may be read as 'raw-rice, overcooked and burnt' (three faults) or with apakvataṇḍula as one item; the sense is the same.

hindi: और जो मन को रुचिकर न हो, वह हृदय-विरुद्ध कहा जाता है। सम्पत्-विरुद्ध उसे जानना चाहिए जिसका रस उत्पन्न न हुआ हो,
english: And what is not pleasing to the mind is called incompatible with the heart (hṛd). One should know as incompatible with excellence (sampad) that whose taste has not developed,
notes: SENTENCE: the definition of sampad-viruddha continues in 101a.

words.gloss: whose taste has passed its time

words.gram: n. nom. sg., ppp. caus. upa-√yuj

hindi: या जिसका रस बीत चुका हो, या जिसका रस बिगड़ ही गया हो। और विधि-विरुद्ध उसे जानना चाहिए जो एकान्त में नहीं खाया जाता। इस प्रकार का अन्न प्रयोग किए जाने पर विरुद्ध होता है।
english: or whose taste has passed its time, or whose taste is indeed spoiled. And to be known as incompatible with the rule (vidhi) is what is not eaten in privacy. Food of such kinds, when used, would be incompatible.
notes: SENTENCE: 101a completes 100b. evaṃvidham is taken as one word 'of such kind'.
lines_deva: ज्ञेयं विधिविरुद्धं तु भुज्यते निभृते न यत्
lines_iast: jñeyaṃ vidhiviruddhaṃ tu bhujyate nibhṛte na yat

words.gloss: of impotence, blindness, vīsarpa and dakodara
of fainting, intoxication, ādhmāna and galagraha

hindi: विरुद्ध अन्न को नपुंसकता, अन्धता, वीसर्प, दकोदर, विस्फोटक, उन्माद, भगन्दर, मूर्च्छा, मद, आध्मान, गलग्रह, पाण्डु रोग और आमविष का,
english: (Incompatible food, they declare, is the cause) of impotence (ṣāṇḍhya), blindness, vīsarpa, dakodara, visphoṭaka, insanity (unmāda), bhagandara, mūrcchā (fainting), mada (intoxication), ādhmāna, galagraha, the disease pāṇḍu, and āmaviṣa,
notes: SENTENCE: 102 and 103 form one sentence; the verb pravadanti is in 103b. Upajāti (indravajrā) metre; vīsarpa with long ī is required by the metre. dakodara is taken as daka-udara (udara with water); āmaviṣa as 'āma-poison'; names kept Sanskrit, no modern identifications. The gender given for the mixed dvandvas follows the last member.

words.gloss: of kilāsa, kuṣṭha and grahaṇī disease
of swelling, amlapitta, fever and pīnasa

hindi: किलास, कुष्ठ और ग्रहणी रोग का, शोथ, अम्लपित्त, ज्वर और पीनस का, सन्तान-दोष का और उसी प्रकार मृत्यु का कारण बताते हैं।
english: of kilāsa, kuṣṭha and grahaṇī disease, of swelling (śotha), amlapitta, fever (jvara) and pīnasa, of defects in offspring, and likewise of death.
notes: SENTENCE: completes 102. grahaṇī-gada may also be read with gada governing all three ('the diseases kilāsa, kuṣṭha and grahaṇī'). Disease names kept Sanskrit.

hindi: इन और अन्य विरोध-जनित रोगों के ये भाव प्रतिकार हैं — जैसे वमन और विरेचन, और उनके विरोधी द्रव्यों का शमन के लिए प्रयोग, तथा वैसे द्रव्यों से पहले ही शरीर का संस्कार।
english: Of these and of other diseases caused by incompatibility, the following are the remedies: namely, emesis and purgation, the use of substances opposed to those (incompatibles) for pacifying them, and the prior conditioning of the body with substances of that kind.
notes: This unit is prose typed as two verse lines (no metre). tadvirodhinām is taken as 'opposed to those (incompatible things)'; it may also mean 'opposed to those (diseases)'.
lines_deva: एषां खल्वपरेषां च वैरोधिकनिमित्तानां व्याधीनामिमे भावाः प्रतिकारा भवन्ति
तद्यथा वमनं विरेचनं च तद्विरोधिनां च द्रव्याणां संशमनार्थमुपयोगः तथाविधैश्च द्रव्यैः पूर्वमभिसंस्कारः शरीरस्येति
lines_iast: eṣāṃ khalvapareṣāṃ ca vairodhikanimittānāṃ vyādhīnāmime bhāvāḥ pratikārā bhavanti
tadyathā vamanaṃ virecanaṃ ca tadvirodhināṃ ca dravyāṇāṃ saṃśamanārthamupayogaḥ tathāvidhaiśca dravyaiḥ pūrvamabhisaṃskāraḥ śarīrasyeti

hindi: और यहाँ दो (श्लोक) हैं: विरुद्ध भोजन से उत्पन्न रोगों को विवेचन, वमन और शमन, अथवा पहले से हितकर का सेवन नष्ट करता है।
english: And here there are two: Purgation (vivecana), emesis and pacifying (śamana), or the prior use of what is wholesome, counters diseases born of incompatible eating.
notes: The singular verb pratihanti goes with each of the listed measures. vivecana (literally 'separating out') is taken as purgation, since emesis is named separately. The parallel list in 104 (vamana, virecana, saṃśamana, prior conditioning) supports vivecana = virecana.
lines_deva: वमनं शमनं चैव पूर्वं वा हितसेवनम्
lines_iast: vamanaṃ śamanaṃ caiva pūrvaṃ vā hitasevanam

words.gloss: for one with keen digestive fire
for the unctuous, exercised and strong
words.gram: m. gen. pl., compound in -balin (dvandva of qualities, or tat-puruṣa 'strong through unction and exercise'; see notes)

hindi: सात्म्य होने से, अथवा अल्प मात्रा में होने से भी, और प्रदीप्त अग्नि वाले तथा युवा के लिए, तथा स्निग्ध, व्यायाम करने वाले और बलवान लोगों के लिए विरुद्ध निष्फल हो जाता है।
english: Through suitability (sātmya), or also through small quantity, and for one with keen digestive fire and the young, and for those who are unctuous, used to exercise and strong, the incompatible becomes ineffective.
notes: snigdha-vyāyāma-balinām may also be read 'for those strong through unction and exercise'. vitatha literally 'untrue, futile'.

hindi: यहाँ श्लोक हैं: रस-निर्णय के विषय में महर्षियों का जो-जो मत था; गुण और कर्म के अनुसार द्रव्य; रस पर आश्रित द्रव्य-संख्या;
english: Here, the verses: whatever opinion the great sages each held on the determination of taste; substances by their qualities and actions; the number of substances based on taste;

text_flags.why: krama + bhyām would give kramābhyām, so the printed form is not grammatical; guṇakarman (quality and action) appears in 110 of this chunk (guṇakarmaṇi); metre: printed syllables 5-7 ṇa kra ma = – ⏑ –, with karmabhyāṃ ṇa kar ma = ⏑ – –, the normal odd-pāda pattern (8 syllables either way)

notes: SENTENCE: the summary verses 107-113 form one sentence, a list of topics ending in 113 'all that the sage told in the Ātreyabhadrakāpyīya'.

words.gloss: the characteristic of rasa and anurasa
words.gram: n. nom. sg., tat-puruṣa (dvandva first member)

hindi: रसों की संख्या का कारण; रस और अनुरस का लक्षण; और पर आदि गुणों के अलग-अलग लक्षण;
english: the reason for the number of tastes; the characteristic of rasa and anurasa (subsidiary taste); and the characteristics of the qualities beginning with para, each separately;

hindi: और जिस कारण से पञ्चात्मक रस छह हैं; और जिस गुण की अधिकता से रस ऊर्ध्वगामी और अनुलोमगामी होते हैं;
english: the reason by which the tastes, being composed of the five (pañcātmaka), are six; and from the excess of which quality the tastes tend upward or downward;
lines_deva: पञ्चात्मकानां षट्त्वं च रसानां येन हेतुना
lines_iast: pañcātmakānāṃ ṣaṭtvaṃ ca rasānāṃ yena hetunā

hindi: छह रसों के षट्त्व के विषय में उप-विभागों सहित विभाग; और द्रव्यों के गुण-कर्म के विषय में उद्देश और अपवाद;
english: the divisions, with their subdivisions, regarding the sixfoldness of the six tastes; and the general statement and the exception about the quality and action of substances;
notes: savibhaktāḥ 'with their subdivisions' is a literal rendering; what the divisions are is not stated in this chunk.
lines_deva: षण्णां रसानां षट्त्वे च सविभक्ता विभक्तयः
lines_iast: ṣaṇṇāṃ rasānāṃ ṣaṭtve ca savibhaktā vibhaktayaḥ

words.gloss: determination of the number of potencies

hindi: गुरुता आदि में रसों का श्रेष्ठ, अवर और मध्य होना; पाक और प्रभाव का लक्षण; वीर्य-संख्या का निश्चय;
english: the highest, lowest and middle rank of the tastes in heaviness and the rest; the sign of pāka (vipāka, post-digestive taste) and prabhāva (specific action); the determination of the number of vīryas (potencies);

text_flags.why: gaurva is not a word (gaurava 'heaviness'); with gaurva the pāda has 7 syllables, with gaurava the required 8 (ra sā nāṃ gau ra vā di ṣu: syllables 5-7 ra vā di = ⏑ – ⏑, as an even pāda requires)

notes: rasānām is printed with m before a consonant (for ṃ); this is only spelling and is kept.

words.gram: m. gen. pl., pres. pass. part. caus. ā-√svad

hindi: चखे जाते हुए छह रसों का जो स्वलक्षण है; जो-जो जिससे विरुद्ध होता है, जिसके द्वारा, और जो जिस कार्य को करने वाला है;
english: the own characteristic (svalakṣaṇa) of the six tastes as they are tasted; whatever is incompatible with whatever, through what, and what each one produces;
notes: The relative clauses in 112b are compressed; yasmāt is taken as 'with what' (the thing it conflicts with) and yena as 'through what (cause)'.

hindi: और विरोध से उत्पन्न रोगों की जो औषध है — वह सब मुनि ने आत्रेयभद्रकाप्यीय में कहा।
english: and the medicine for diseases caused by incompatibility: all that the sage told in the Ātreyabhadrakāpyīya.

text_flags.why: vyāhīnām is not a word; the same phrase vairodhikanimittānāṃ vyādhīnām is printed in 104 of this chunk

notes: avadan is avadat before muniḥ (t becomes n before a nasal); no error. Chapter name in -īya kept unsplit.

hindi: इस प्रकार अग्निवेश द्वारा रचित, चरक द्वारा प्रतिसंस्कृत तन्त्र के श्लोकस्थान में आत्रेयभद्रकाप्यीय नामक छब्बीसवाँ अध्याय।
english: Thus, in the treatise composed by Agniveśa and redacted by Caraka, in the Śloka section (Ślokasthāna), the twenty-sixth chapter named Ātreyabhadrakāpyīya.
notes: Chapter colophon (prose).
lines_deva: इत्यग्निवेशकृते तन्त्रे चरकप्रतिसंस्कृते श्लोकस्थाने आत्रेयभद्रकाप्यीयो नाम षड्विंशोऽध्यायः
lines_iast: ityagniveśakṛte tantre carakapratisaṃskṛte ślokasthāne ātreyabhadrakāpyīyo nāma ṣaḍviṃśo'dhyāyaḥ
